<section id="S1" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">Appendix A </span>Code Availability</h2>

<div id="S1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The code used in this study is available at <a href="https://github.com/williamgilpin/icicl" title="" class="ltx_ref ltx_url ltx_font_typewriter">https://github.com/williamgilpin/icicl</a></p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S2" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">Appendix B </span>Model architecture and training</h2>

<section id="S2.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">A </span>Architecture</h3>

<div id="S2.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We implement a compact causal language model operating on a discrete vocabulary (<math id="S2.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="V=100" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>V</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>100</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">V=100</annotation></semantics></math>) that predicts the next token autoregressively. Our model is a decoder-only transformer, similar to GPT models but with relative positional embedding akin to the T5 family <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib39" title="" class="ltx_ref">7</a>, <a href="#bib.bib9" title="" class="ltx_ref">28</a>]</cite>. Each input token is mapped to a higher-dimensional embedding (<math id="S2.SS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d_{\text{model}}=256" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>d</mi><mtext>model</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>256</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_{\text{model}}=256</annotation></semantics></math>). The network itself consists of two identical Transformer-style residual blocks, each using single-head causal self-attention, with query and key projections into <math id="S2.SS1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d_{k}=128" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>128</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_{k}=128</annotation></semantics></math> dimensions, and a value projection back into <math id="S2.SS1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d_{\text{model}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>d</mi><mtext>model</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_{\text{model}}</annotation></semantics></math> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib13" title="" class="ltx_ref">36</a>]</cite>. Attention logits are scaled by <math id="S2.SS1.p1.m5" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="d_{k}^{-1/2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>d</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mi>k</mi></msub><msup><mrow></mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_{k}^{-1/2}</annotation></semantics></math> and strictly masked with a lower-triangular causal mask. Each block applies pre-normalization with LayerNorm before attention <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib12" title="" class="ltx_ref">4</a>]</cite>, then adds the attention output residually, and then applies a second LayerNorm followed by a position-wise feed-forward network with expansion factor <math id="S2.SS1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2</annotation></semantics></math> (resulting in hidden width <math id="S2.SS1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2d_{\text{model}}=512" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mtext>model</mtext></msub></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>512</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2d_{\text{model}}=512</annotation></semantics></math>), using ReLU activation and a second linear layer returning to <math id="S2.SS1.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d_{\text{model}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>d</mi><mtext>model</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_{\text{model}}</annotation></semantics></math>, again added residually.
A final LayerNorm precedes the output projection to logits over the vocabulary. The output projection is weight-tied to the input embedding matrix. The maximum context length is a fixed block size of <math id="S2.SS1.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T_{\max}=512" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>T</mi><mi>max</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>512</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T_{\max}=512</annotation></semantics></math> tokens. Positional information is encoded using ALiBi, an additive attention-logit bias proportional to the nonnegative lag distance with slope <math id="S2.SS1.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha=1.0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1.0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha=1.0</annotation></semantics></math>, i.e. a term <math id="S2.SS1.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-\alpha\,(i-j)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo lspace="0.170em">⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-\alpha\,(i-j)</annotation></semantics></math> for <math id="S2.SS1.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i\geq j" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>≥</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i\geq j</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S2.SS1.p1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0</annotation></semantics></math> otherwise.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S2.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">B </span>Tokenization</h3>

<div id="S2.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We convert real-valued time series into tokens with mean scaling followed by uniform scalar quantization into <math id="S2.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="V" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>V</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">V</annotation></semantics></math> bins, following the approach used in the first generation of the Chronos family of time series foundation models <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib35" title="" class="ltx_ref">3</a>]</cite>.
We favor direct quantization over patch-based approaches used in other time series foundation models due to the interpretability of the token space, and because it allows us to design our study based on prior studies of in-context generalization in language models <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib38" title="" class="ltx_ref">15</a>]</cite>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S2.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Given training time series <math id="S2.SS2.p2.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="x_{1:T}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x_{1:T}</annotation></semantics></math> of length <math id="S2.SS2.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>T</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T</annotation></semantics></math>, we compute a scale factor from the context</p>
<table id="S2.Ex1" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S2.Ex1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s=\max\!\left(\frac{1}{T}\sum_{i=1}^{T}\lvert x_{i}\rvert,\ \varepsilon\right),\qquad\varepsilon=10^{-8}," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mpadded style="width:1.808em;" width="1.808em"><mi>max</mi></mpadded><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>T</mi></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><munderover><mo movablelimits="false" rspace="0em">∑</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>T</mi></munderover><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.667em">,</mo><mi>ε</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mrow><mi>ε</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s=\max\!\left(\frac{1}{T}\sum_{i=1}^{T}\lvert x_{i}\rvert,\ \varepsilon\right),\qquad\varepsilon=10^{-8},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S2.SS2.p2.2" class="ltx_p">and we then normalize the entire series <math id="S2.SS2.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{x}_{i}=x_{i}/s" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>x</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>/</mo><mi>s</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tilde{x}_{i}=x_{i}/s</annotation></semantics></math>. The normalized values are discretized into integer bin IDs in <math id="S2.SS2.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{1,\dots,V\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>V</mi><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{1,\dots,V\}</annotation></semantics></math> using uniformly spaced bin centers <math id="S2.SS2.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c_{j}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c_{j}</annotation></semantics></math> spanning <math id="S2.SS2.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[c_{\min},c_{\max}]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>min</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>max</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[c_{\min},c_{\max}]</annotation></semantics></math> (with <math id="S2.SS2.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c_{\min}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>min</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c_{\min}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S2.SS2.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c_{\max}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>max</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c_{\max}</annotation></semantics></math> treated as hyperparameters), and decision boundaries placed at midpoints between adjacent centers, with outer edges extending to <math id="S2.SS2.p2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pm\infty" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>±</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pm\infty</annotation></semantics></math> so that all values map to a unique bin. A reserved <span id="S2.SS2.p2.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-quote ltx_outerquote">“padding”</span> token uses ID <math id="S2.SS2.p2.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0</annotation></semantics></math>.
Missing values (NaNs) are handled by replacing their contribution with <math id="S2.SS2.p2.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0</annotation></semantics></math> for purposes of scale computation, while their token positions are set to the padding ID <math id="S2.SS2.p2.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0</annotation></semantics></math> in the emitted token sequence.
Decoding maps bin IDs back to their corresponding centers and rescales via <math id="S2.SS2.p2.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{x}_{i}=s\,\tilde{x}_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>x</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>x</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{x}_{i}=s\,\tilde{x}_{i}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S2.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">C </span>Training</h3>

<div id="S2.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We train our model using next-token prediction with cross-entropy loss over the vocabulary. We quantize the training time series and provide it to the model as a single long one-dimensional token stream, from which we sample fixed-length windows of length <math id="S2.SS3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T=512" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>512</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T=512</annotation></semantics></math> uniformly at random: the input is a contiguous block of <math id="S2.SS3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="512" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>512</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">512</annotation></semantics></math> tokens and the target is the same block shifted by one position. The effective dataset length is treated as a large virtual size (<math id="S2.SS3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="10,000" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>10,000</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10,000</annotation></semantics></math> samples) with random window sampling each time. We optimize the model using AdamW with learning rate <math id="S2.SS3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="5\times 10^{-5}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>5</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">5\times 10^{-5}</annotation></semantics></math>, weight decay <math id="S2.SS3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.0</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.0</annotation></semantics></math>, batch size <math id="S2.SS3.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="32" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>32</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">32</annotation></semantics></math>, with gradient accumulation over micro-batches (with default size <math id="S2.SS3.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1</annotation></semantics></math>) by averaging loss across micro-steps before backpropagation <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib10" title="" class="ltx_ref">22</a>]</cite>.
We clip gradients to a maximum global norm of <math id="S2.SS3.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1.0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1.0</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.0</annotation></semantics></math> at each step. We train for <math id="S2.SS3.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="50,000" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>50,000</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">50,000</annotation></semantics></math> optimization steps and perform validation every <math id="S2.SS3.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1000" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1000</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1000</annotation></semantics></math> steps by evaluating cross-entropy on one randomly sampled validation batch, and additionally on a separate out-of-distribution validation stream of the same form. We do not use a learning-rate schedule.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S2.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">D </span>Inference</h3>

<div id="S2.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We perform autoregressive inference for a specified number of new tokens <math id="S2.SS4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>H</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H</annotation></semantics></math> beyond the provided context. At each step, we use only the most recent <math id="S2.SS4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C=512" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>512</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C=512</annotation></semantics></math> context tokens. The model outputs logits for the next token, which are converted to a token choice either greedily (argmax, temperature <math id="S2.SS4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0</annotation></semantics></math>) or by sampling.
We append the sampled token to the context, and repeat the process for <math id="S2.SS4.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>H</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H</annotation></semantics></math> steps, yielding a lengthened token sequence.
If a real-valued time series is needed for downstream analysis, we decode the output token sequence back to real values via dequantization to bin centers followed by multiplication by the stored mean scale <math id="S2.SS4.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>s</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S3" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">Appendix C </span>Estimating the fully-observed transfer operator with Ulam’s method</h2>

<div id="S3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Let <math id="S3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{\mathbf{y}_{t}\}_{t=0}^{N-1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>𝐲</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{\mathbf{y}_{t}\}_{t=0}^{N-1}</annotation></semantics></math> be a time series (discrete-time) sampled at uniform intervals <math id="S3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math> from a trajectory <math id="S3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{y}(t)\in\mathbb{R}^{D}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>𝐲</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>D</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{y}(t)\in\mathbb{R}^{D}</annotation></semantics></math> in the fully-observed phase space. We construct a finite-rank approximation of the Perron-Frobenius (transfer) operator at lag <math id="S3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>τ</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math> by (1) partitioning the <math id="S3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>D</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D</annotation></semantics></math>-dimensional phase space into <math id="S3.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math> bins, (2) symbolizing the trajectory by bin labels, and (3) estimating the induced Markov transition matrix between bins.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Partition and symbolic dynamics.</span> We partition <math id="S3.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{B_{1},\dots,B_{K}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>B</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>B</mi><mi>K</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{B_{1},\dots,B_{K}\}</annotation></semantics></math> the data <math id="S3.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{\mathbf{y}_{t}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>𝐲</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{\mathbf{y}_{t}\}</annotation></semantics></math> by clustering. Given a set of samples <math id="S3.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{\mathbf{y}_{t}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>𝐲</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{\mathbf{y}_{t}\}</annotation></semantics></math> we use <math id="S3.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math>-means clustering to generate Voronoi cells <math id="S3.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B_{i}\equiv\{\mathbf{y}:\arg\min_{j}\|\mathbf{y}-\mathbf{c}_{j}\|=i\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>B</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>≡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mi>𝐲</mi><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>arg</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><msub><mi>min</mi><mi>j</mi></msub></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mi>𝐲</mi><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>𝐜</mi><mi>j</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B_{i}\equiv\{\mathbf{y}:\arg\min_{j}\|\mathbf{y}-\mathbf{c}_{j}\|=i\}</annotation></semantics></math> with centers <math id="S3.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{\mathbf{c}_{i}\}_{i=1}^{K}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>𝐜</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>K</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{\mathbf{c}_{i}\}_{i=1}^{K}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S3.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{c}_{i}\in\mathbb{R}^{D}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝐜</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>D</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{c}_{i}\in\mathbb{R}^{D}</annotation></semantics></math>. This defines a (hard) coding map <math id="S3.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\kappa:\mathbf{y}\to\{1,\dots,K\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>κ</mi><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mi>𝐲</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>K</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\kappa:\mathbf{y}\to\{1,\dots,K\}</annotation></semantics></math>, which we apply to the training data to generate the symbolic sequence</p>
<table id="S3.Ex2" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.Ex2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s_{t}\;:=\;\kappa(\mathbf{y}_{t})\in\{1,\dots,K\}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.558em" rspace="0.558em">:=</mo><mrow><mi>κ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝐲</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>K</mi><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s_{t}\;:=\;\kappa(\mathbf{y}_{t})\in\{1,\dots,K\}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="S3.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Empirical Ulam matrix at lag <math id="S3.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math>.</span> For a fixed lag <math id="S3.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math>, Ulam’s method approximates the transfer operator <math id="S3.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{P}_{\tau}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><mi>τ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{P}_{\tau}</annotation></semantics></math> by the <math id="S3.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K\times K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>K</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K\times K</annotation></semantics></math> matrix <math id="S3.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P^{(\tau)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>P</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>τ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P^{(\tau)}</annotation></semantics></math> as</p>
<table id="S3.Ex3" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.Ex3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P^{(\tau)}_{ij}\;\approx\;\mathbb{P}(s_{t+\tau}=j\mid s_{t}=i)," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>P</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>τ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo lspace="0.558em" rspace="0.558em">≈</mo><mrow><mi>ℙ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>s</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>τ</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mrow><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P^{(\tau)}_{ij}\;\approx\;\mathbb{P}(s_{t+\tau}=j\mid s_{t}=i),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.p3.2" class="ltx_p">i.e., the probability mass transferred from bin <math id="S3.p3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>B</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> to bin <math id="S3.p3.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B_{j}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>B</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B_{j}</annotation></semantics></math> over time <math id="S3.p3.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math>. We compute this quantity by counting all transition pairs, and dividing by the total number of transitions.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Estimating the transfer operator spectrum.</span> Once <math id="S3.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P^{(\tau)}\in\mathbb{R}^{K\times K}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>P</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>τ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>K</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P^{(\tau)}\in\mathbb{R}^{K\times K}</annotation></semantics></math> is obtained, we treat it as a Markov operator. We estimate the stationary distribution <math id="S3.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi^{(0)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>π</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi^{(0)}</annotation></semantics></math> from the invariant left eigenvector of <math id="S3.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P^{(\tau)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>P</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>τ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P^{(\tau)}</annotation></semantics></math>,</p>
<table id="S3.Ex4" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.Ex4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi^{\top}P^{(\tau)}=\pi^{\top},\qquad\sum_{i=1}^{K}\pi_{i}=1,\qquad\pi_{i}\geq 0." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>π</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>P</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>τ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup></mrow><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>π</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup></mrow><mo rspace="2.000em">,</mo><mrow><mrow><munderover><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>K</mi></munderover><msub><mi>π</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>π</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>≥</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi^{\top}P^{(\tau)}=\pi^{\top},\qquad\sum_{i=1}^{K}\pi_{i}=1,\qquad\pi_{i}\geq 0.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.p4.2" class="ltx_p">We solve this using power iteration on <math id="S3.p4.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(P^{(\tau)})^{\top}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>P</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>τ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>⊤</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(P^{(\tau)})^{\top}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.p5.1" class="ltx_p">We estimate long-lived transient modes <math id="S3.p5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi^{(i)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>π</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi^{(i)}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S3.p5.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math> by applying power iteration to a deflated operator that removes the stationary mode. Writing <math id="S3.p5.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>𝟏</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{1}</annotation></semantics></math> for the all-ones vector, the deflation</p>
<table id="S3.Ex5" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.Ex5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\widetilde{P}^{(\tau)}\;=\;P^{(\tau)}-\mathbf{1}\,\pi^{\top}" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mover accent="true"><mi>P</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>τ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0.558em" rspace="0.558em">=</mo><mrow><msup><mi>P</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>τ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo>−</mo><mrow><mn>𝟏</mn><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>π</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\widetilde{P}^{(\tau)}\;=\;P^{(\tau)}-\mathbf{1}\,\pi^{\top}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.p5.2" class="ltx_p">annihilates the stationary left eigenvector and allows us to estimate the leading subdominant left modes (metastable transients) with power iteration.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.p6" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.p6.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.p6.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Choice of partition size.</span> Because Ulam discretization trades bias (too few bins) against variance/sparsity (too many bins), we scan over candidate <math id="S3.p6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math> and select a value that yields informative, non-degenerate transition structure. We compute a row-wise entropy statistic of <math id="S3.p6.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P^{(\tau)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>P</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>τ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P^{(\tau)}</annotation></semantics></math> across <math id="S3.p6.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math> and choose values that maximize this statistic. This heuristic favors partitions that are neither so large that most transitions are self-loops, nor so small that the transition matrix becomes overly sparse.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">Appendix D </span>Estimating the manifold dimension of the Lorenz-96 system</h2>

<div id="S4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We consider the <math id="S4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>D</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D</annotation></semantics></math>-dimensional Lorenz-96 system with constant forcing,</p>
<table id="S4.E1" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.E1.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\dot{X_{i}}=(X_{i+1}-X_{i-2})X_{i-1}-X_{i}+F,\qquad i=1,\dots,D," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><msub><mi>X</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>˙</mo></mover><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>X</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>X</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><msub><mi>X</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>X</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><mi>F</mi><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>D</mi><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\dot{X_{i}}=(X_{i+1}-X_{i-2})X_{i-1}-X_{i}+F,\qquad i=1,\dots,D,</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(A1)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S4.p1.2" class="ltx_p">with cyclic boundary conditions <math id="S4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="X_{i+n}=X_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>X</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>X</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">X_{i+n}=X_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="X_{i-n}=X_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>X</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>X</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">X_{i-n}=X_{i}</annotation></semantics></math>. Here <math id="S4.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="X_{i}(t)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>X</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">X_{i}(t)</annotation></semantics></math> are the state variables, <math id="S4.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>D</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D</annotation></semantics></math> is the system dimension, and <math id="S4.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="F" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>F</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">F</annotation></semantics></math> is the constant external forcing. In all simulations we set <math id="S4.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="F=8.0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>F</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>8.0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">F=8.0</annotation></semantics></math>. The initial condition is taken as <math id="S4.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="X_{i}(0)=F" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>X</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>F</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">X_{i}(0)=F</annotation></semantics></math> for all <math id="S4.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>i</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i</annotation></semantics></math>, with a random normal perturbation of <math id="S4.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="10^{-2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10^{-2}</annotation></semantics></math> added to the first component to ensure diversity across generated trajectories. The system is integrated to <math id="S4.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1000" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1000</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1000</annotation></semantics></math> time units using the implicit Radau IIA method. We discard the first 500 steps of the generated trajectory as transients.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Given a multivariate time series <math id="S4.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{\mathbf{y}_{i}\}_{i=1}^{N}\subset\mathbb{R}^{D}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>𝐲</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>N</mi></msubsup><mo>⊂</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>D</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{\mathbf{y}_{i}\}_{i=1}^{N}\subset\mathbb{R}^{D}</annotation></semantics></math>, the Grassberger-Procaccia calculation is implemented by first forming the full matrix of pairwise Euclidean distances <math id="S4.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho_{ij}=\lVert\mathbf{y}_{i}-\mathbf{y}_{j}\rVert_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>ρ</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo rspace="0.1389em">=</mo><msub><mrow><mo fence="true" lspace="0.1389em" rspace="0em">∥</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝐲</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>𝐲</mi><mi>j</mi></msub></mrow><mo fence="true" lspace="0em">∥</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho_{ij}=\lVert\mathbf{y}_{i}-\mathbf{y}_{j}\rVert_{2}</annotation></semantics></math> and collecting all strictly positive distances into a single sample <math id="S4.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{\rho_{k}\}_{k=1}^{K}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>ρ</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>K</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{\rho_{k}\}_{k=1}^{K}</annotation></semantics></math> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib20" title="" class="ltx_ref">18</a>]</cite>. To focus on the intermediate scaling regime and reduce the influence of (1) discretization effects at very small separations and (2) finite-size saturation at large separations, the distance sample is truncated by discarding values below the <math id="S4.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>5</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">5</annotation></semantics></math>th percentile and above the <math id="S4.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="50" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>50</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">50</annotation></semantics></math>th percentile. The remaining distances are treated as draws from a power-law tail <math id="S4.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p(\rho)\propto\rho^{-\alpha}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ρ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>∝</mo><msup><mi>ρ</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>α</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p(\rho)\propto\rho^{-\alpha}</annotation></semantics></math> for <math id="S4.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho\geq\rho_{\min}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ρ</mi><mo>≥</mo><msub><mi>ρ</mi><mi>min</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho\geq\rho_{\min}</annotation></semantics></math>, where <math id="S4.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho_{\min}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>ρ</mi><mi>min</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho_{\min}</annotation></semantics></math> is taken as the minimum retained distance, and the exponent is estimated by the continuous maximum-likelihood formula <math id="S4.p2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\widehat{\alpha}=1+\left[\frac{1}{K}\sum_{k=1}^{K}\ln\!\left(\rho_{k}/\rho_{\min}\right)\right]^{-1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>α</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><msup><mrow><mo>[</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>K</mi></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><msubsup><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>K</mi></msubsup><mrow><mpadded style="width:0.748em;" width="0.748em"><mi>ln</mi></mpadded><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>ρ</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>/</mo><msub><mi>ρ</mi><mi>min</mi></msub></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>]</mo></mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\widehat{\alpha}=1+\left[\frac{1}{K}\sum_{k=1}^{K}\ln\!\left(\rho_{k}/\rho_{\min}\right)\right]^{-1}</annotation></semantics></math> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib22" title="" class="ltx_ref">10</a>]</cite>. This scaling exponent is interpreted as the manifold dimension <math id="S4.p2.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d_{\mathcal{M}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>d</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_{\mathcal{M}}</annotation></semantics></math></p>
</div>
<div id="S4.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.p3.1" class="ltx_p">To measure the scaling of the manifold dimension <math id="S4.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d_{\mathcal{M}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>d</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_{\mathcal{M}}</annotation></semantics></math> with the dynamical dimension <math id="S4.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>D</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D</annotation></semantics></math>, we generate trajectories from the Lorenz-96 system with varying number of dynamical variables <math id="S4.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D=5,6,7...,25" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>,</mo><mrow><mn>7</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi></mrow><mo>,</mo><mn>25</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D=5,6,7...,25</annotation></semantics></math>, and perform the Grassberger-Procaccia algorithm separately for each trajectory (Fig. <a href="#S4.F1" title="Figure S1 ‣ Appendix D Estimating the manifold dimension of the Lorenz-96 system ‣ Transformers for dynamical systems learn transfer operators in-context" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">S1</span></a>). We observe a linear scaling of the manifold dimension <math id="S4.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d_{\mathcal{M}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>d</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_{\mathcal{M}}</annotation></semantics></math> with the dynamical dimension <math id="S4.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>D</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S4.F1" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2602.18679v1/sfig_lorenz96.png" id="S4.F1.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:381/188;" width="381" height="188" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure S1: </span>
The estimated manifold dimension <math id="S4.F1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d_{\mathcal{M}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>d</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_{\mathcal{M}}</annotation></semantics></math> of the attractor of the Lorenz-96 system as the number of dynamical variables <math id="S4.F1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>D</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D</annotation></semantics></math> varies.
</figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
<section id="S5" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">Appendix E </span>Attention rollout</h2>

<div id="S5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For a fixed context length <math id="S5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>C</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C</annotation></semantics></math> and an input token sequence <math id="S5.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{x}_{C}\in\mathbb{Z}^{C}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>C</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℤ</mi><mi>C</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{x}_{C}\in\mathbb{Z}^{C}</annotation></semantics></math>, let <math id="S5.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A^{(\ell)}(\mathbf{x}_{C})\in\mathbb{R}^{C\times C}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>A</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>C</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>C</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A^{(\ell)}(\mathbf{x}_{C})\in\mathbb{R}^{C\times C}</annotation></semantics></math> denote the causal self-attention matrix produced by layer <math id="S5.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell\in\{1,\dots,L\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>L</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell\in\{1,\dots,L\}</annotation></semantics></math> (though we set <math id="S5.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L=2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L=2</annotation></semantics></math> in our experiments), where each row is a probability distribution over past positions (row-stochastic under the softmax and causal mask). Following <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib5" title="" class="ltx_ref">1</a>]</cite>, we incorporate residual mixing by defining the augmented layer-wise transition</p>
<table id="S5.E2" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S5.E2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\widetilde{A}^{(\ell)}(\mathbf{x}_{C})\;=\;I+A^{(\ell)}(\mathbf{x}_{C})," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msup><mover accent="true"><mi>A</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>C</mi></msub><mo rspace="0.280em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.558em">=</mo><mrow><mi>I</mi><mo>+</mo><mrow><msup><mi>A</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>C</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\widetilde{A}^{(\ell)}(\mathbf{x}_{C})\;=\;I+A^{(\ell)}(\mathbf{x}_{C}),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(A2)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S5.p1.2" class="ltx_p">and propagate attention through depth by matrix multiplication,</p>
<table id="S5.E3" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S5.E3.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="A_{\mathrm{roll}}(\mathbf{x}_{C})\;=\;\widetilde{A}^{(L)}(\mathbf{x}_{C})\,\widetilde{A}^{(L-1)}(\mathbf{x}_{C})\cdots\widetilde{A}^{(1)}(\mathbf{x}_{C})\;\in\;\mathbb{R}^{C\times C}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>roll</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>C</mi></msub><mo rspace="0.280em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.558em">=</mo><msup><mover accent="true"><mi>A</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>L</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>C</mi></msub><mo rspace="0.170em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><msup><mover accent="true"><mi>A</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>C</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋯</mo><msup><mover accent="true"><mi>A</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>C</mi></msub><mo rspace="0.280em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.558em">∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>C</mi></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A_{\mathrm{roll}}(\mathbf{x}_{C})\;=\;\widetilde{A}^{(L)}(\mathbf{x}_{C})\,\widetilde{A}^{(L-1)}(\mathbf{x}_{C})\cdots\widetilde{A}^{(1)}(\mathbf{x}_{C})\;\in\;\mathbb{R}^{C\times C}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(A3)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S5.p1.3" class="ltx_p">The entry <math id="S5.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(A_{\mathrm{roll}})_{ij}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>roll</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(A_{\mathrm{roll}})_{ij}</annotation></semantics></math> can be interpreted as the effective contribution (via all compositional attention paths across layers) of token position <math id="S5.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="j" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>j</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">j</annotation></semantics></math> to the representation at position <math id="S5.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>i</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i</annotation></semantics></math>. In practice, we average <math id="S5.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A_{\mathrm{roll}}(\mathbf{x}_{C})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>roll</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>C</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A_{\mathrm{roll}}(\mathbf{x}_{C})</annotation></semantics></math> across the Test-OOD contexts to obtain a single rollout matrix <math id="S5.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A_{\mathrm{roll}}\in\mathbb{R}^{C\times C}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>roll</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>C</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A_{\mathrm{roll}}\in\mathbb{R}^{C\times C}</annotation></semantics></math> summarizing how the trained model distributes influence across lags; we then quantify its effective dimensionality using the stable rank <math id="S5.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d_{\mathrm{latent}}=\mathrm{srank}(A_{\mathrm{roll}})=\|A_{\mathrm{roll}}\|_{F}^{2}/\|A_{\mathrm{roll}}\|_{2}^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>latent</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>srank</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>roll</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>roll</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mi>F</mi><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo>/</mo><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>roll</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn><mn>2</mn></msubsup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_{\mathrm{latent}}=\mathrm{srank}(A_{\mathrm{roll}})=\|A_{\mathrm{roll}}\|_{F}^{2}/\|A_{\mathrm{roll}}\|_{2}^{2}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
</section>

              d="M224 160C224 107 267 64 320 64C373 64 416 107 416 160L416 163.6C416 179.3 403.3 192 387.6 192L252.5 192C236.8 192 224.1 179.3 224.1 163.6L224.1 160zM569.6 172.8C580.2 186.9 577.3 207 563.2 217.6L465.4 290.9C470.7 299.8 474.7 309.6 477.2 320L576 320C593.7 320 608 334.3 608 352C608 369.7 593.7 384 576 384L480 384L480 416C480 418.6 479.9 421.3 479.8 423.9L563.2 486.4C577.3 497 580.2 517.1 569.6 531.2C559 545.3 538.9 548.2 524.8 537.6L461.7 490.3C438.5 534.5 395.2 566.5 344 574.2L344 344C344 330.7 333.3 320 320 320C306.7 320 296 330.7 296 344L296 574.2C244.8 566.5 201.5 534.5 178.3 490.3L115.2 537.6C101.1 548.2 81 545.3 70.4 531.2C59.8 517.1 62.7 497 76.8 486.4L160.2 423.9C160.1 421.3 160 418.7 160 416L160 384L64 384C46.3 384 32 369.7 32 352C32 334.3 46.3 320 64 320L162.8 320C165.3 309.6 169.3 299.8 174.6 290.9L76.8 217.6C62.7 207 59.8 186.9 70.4 172.8C81 158.7 101.1 155.8 115.2 166.4L224 248C236.3 242.9 249.8 240 264 240L376 240C390.2 240 403.7 242.8 416 248L524.8 166.4C538.9 155.8 559 158.7 569.6 172.8z" />
          </svg>)</span> button, located in the page header.</li>
    </ul>
    <p><strong>Tip:</strong> You can select the relevant text first, to include it in your report.</p>
    <p>Our team has already identified <a class="ltx_ref" href="https://github.com/arXiv/html_feedback/issues"
        target="_blank">the following issues</a>. We appreciate your time reviewing and reporting rendering errors we
      may not have found yet. Your efforts will help us improve the HTML versions for all readers, because disability
      should not be a barrier to accessing research. Thank you for your continued support in championing open access for
      all.</p>
    <p>Have a free development cycle? Help support accessibility at arXiv! Our collaborators at LaTeXML maintain a <a
        class="ltx_ref" href="https://github.com/brucemiller/LaTeXML/wiki/Porting-LaTeX-packages-for-LaTeXML"
        target="_blank">list of packages that need conversion</a>, and welcome <a class="ltx_ref"
        href="https://github.com/brucemiller/LaTeXML/issues" target="_blank">developer contributions</a>.</p>
